# DSP Architecture: VocalStrip

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-4 implementation. Stage 1 Planning cannot proceed without this file. Stage 3 (DSP) implements this exact architecture.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent)
**Generated date:** 2026-03-20
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Planning), Stage 3 (DSP Implementation)
**Purpose:** DSP specification defining processing components, signal flow, and JUCE module usage

---

## Core Components

### 1. EQ Section: High-Pass Filter (Butterworth)

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>` with `juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makeHighPass()`
- **Purpose:** Remove low-frequency rumble and proximity effect from vocal mic; 2nd-order Butterworth response
- **Parameters Affected:** `eq_hp_freq`, `eq_bypass`
- **Configuration:**
  - Cutoff range: 20–500 Hz, default 80 Hz
  - Order: 2nd-order (single biquad stage) for minimal phase impact
  - Coefficients recalculated on `eq_hp_freq` change and on sample rate change
  - Mono processing only (single-channel filter instance)
  - Coefficient smoothing: update per block (not per sample) to avoid zipper noise on sweep
  - Module: `juce_dsp` required

### 2. EQ Section: Low Shelf Filter

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>` with `juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makeLowShelf()`
- **Purpose:** Boost or cut low body of vocal (200–400 Hz warmth region)
- **Parameters Affected:** `eq_low_shelf_gain`, `eq_low_shelf_freq`, `eq_bypass`
- **Configuration:**
  - Gain range: -12 to +12 dB
  - Frequency range: 60–400 Hz, default 200 Hz
  - Q: Fixed at 0.7071 (Butterworth shelf Q) for gentle, musical slope
  - Coefficients recalculated on gain or frequency change
  - Mono processing

### 3. EQ Section: Mid Peak Filter

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>` with `juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makePeakFilter()`
- **Purpose:** Sweepable bell EQ for presence/body adjustment and resonance notching
- **Parameters Affected:** `eq_mid_gain`, `eq_mid_freq`, `eq_mid_q`, `eq_bypass`
- **Configuration:**
  - Gain range: -12 to +12 dB
  - Frequency range: 200–8000 Hz, default 1000 Hz
  - Q range: 0.3–5.0, default 1.0
  - Three-parameter coefficient recalculation on any change
  - Mono processing

### 4. EQ Section: High Shelf Filter

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>` with `juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makeHighShelf()`
- **Purpose:** Boost or cut high-frequency "air" and brilliance (8–16 kHz)
- **Parameters Affected:** `eq_high_shelf_gain`, `eq_high_shelf_freq`, `eq_bypass`
- **Configuration:**
  - Gain range: -12 to +12 dB
  - Frequency range: 2000–16000 Hz, default 8000 Hz
  - Q: Fixed at 0.7071 for gentle, musical slope
  - Coefficients recalculated on gain or frequency change
  - Mono processing

### 5. Compressor (VCA-style)

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::Compressor<float>`
- **Purpose:** Transparent VCA-style gain reduction for vocal dynamics control
- **Parameters Affected:** `comp_mode`, `comp_amount`, `comp_threshold`, `comp_ratio`, `comp_attack`, `comp_release`, `comp_makeup`, `comp_bypass`
- **Configuration:**
  - Simple mode: `comp_amount` (0–100%) maps to threshold (-40 to -6 dB) and ratio (2:1 to 10:1) curves
    - Threshold formula: `threshold_dB = -6.0f - (amount_normalized * 34.0f)` (amount 0=0%, 1=100%)
    - Ratio formula: `ratio = 2.0f + (amount_normalized * 8.0f)`
    - Attack fixed at 10ms, Release fixed at 200ms in Simple mode
  - Manual mode: All parameters exposed directly
  - Makeup gain: Applied as linear gain post-compressor (`juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain(comp_makeup)`)
  - Module: `juce_dsp` required
  - Mono processing (compressor on mono bus before stereo spread)

### 6. GR Meter Output (Gain Reduction Measurement)

- **JUCE Class:** Custom atomic float updated from audio thread, read by UI timer
- **Purpose:** Feed VU needle GR meter in UI with current gain reduction value in dB
- **Parameters Affected:** `comp_bypass` (bypass = no GR)
- **Configuration:**
  - Audio thread writes `std::atomic<float> grMeterValue` after each processBlock
  - Value range: 0.0 (no reduction) to -30.0 dB (maximum reduction)
  - UI reads via `juce::Timer` at ~30 Hz (not faster - prevents UI thread starvation)
  - Pattern: same as VU meter in critical patterns #20

### 7. Delay Line (Slapback / Sync)

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, juce::dsp::DelayLineInterpolationTypes::Linear>`
- **Purpose:** Single-tap delay for slapback echo or tempo-synced repeat
- **Parameters Affected:** `delay_mode`, `delay_time`, `delay_division`, `delay_feedback`, `delay_mix`, `delay_bypass`
- **Configuration:**
  - Maximum delay: sized for 1/2 note at 40 BPM = 750ms; use 1000ms buffer (48000 samples at 48kHz)
  - Slapback mode: `delay_time` (20–200ms) used directly
  - Sync mode: BPM read from `juce::AudioPlayHead::getPosition()`, division converts to ms
    - 1/16 = (60000/BPM) / 4 ms
    - 1/8  = (60000/BPM) / 2 ms
    - 1/4  = (60000/BPM) ms
    - 1/2  = (60000/BPM) * 2 ms
    - Fallback: 100ms if no AudioPlayHead available
  - Feedback: delay output * `delay_feedback/100.0f` fed back into delay input
  - The delay processes in mono; output is a mono signal mixed with dry mono signal
  - Module: `juce_dsp` required

### 8. Delay Wet/Dry Mixer

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer<float>`
- **Purpose:** Blend dry mono vocal signal with delay wet signal
- **Parameters Affected:** `delay_mix`
- **Configuration:**
  - Mix range: 0–100% maps to 0.0–1.0 wet proportion
  - Uses `MixingRule::linear` (not equal power, to avoid loudness jump at 50%)
  - Operates in mono

### 9. Delay-to-Reverb Send Bus

- **JUCE Class:** Custom implementation (manual buffer copy with gain scaling)
- **Purpose:** Route delay output signal into reverb input at a separate send level
- **Parameters Affected:** `delay_reverb_send`
- **Configuration:**
  - Send point: AFTER delay processing, BEFORE delay wet/dry mix is blended — specifically the delay wet signal (output of delay line after feedback)
  - Send gain: `delay_reverb_send / 100.0f` (linear amplitude)
  - Implementation: accumulate send signal into a temporary mono buffer that is added to the reverb input
  - This creates a parallel path: vocal → delay → (delay wet signal * send level) → reverb input
  - When delay is bypassed: send is also bypassed (no delay output exists)

### 10. Reverb Pre-Delay

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, juce::dsp::DelayLineInterpolationTypes::Linear>`
- **Purpose:** Pre-delay before reverb tail onset (creates sense of space separation)
- **Parameters Affected:** `reverb_predelay`
- **Configuration:**
  - Range: 0–100ms, default 20ms
  - Maximum buffer: 100ms at 192kHz = ~19200 samples (allocate 20000)
  - Stereo pre-delay (two instances, L and R channels after mono-to-stereo expansion)
  - Applied after the mono input is expanded to stereo (by copying mono to both channels)

### 11. Reverb Engine (Plate / Room)

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::Reverb` with custom parameter mapping for Plate vs Room presets
- **Purpose:** Algorithmic stereo reverb with Plate and Room character presets
- **Parameters Affected:** `reverb_type`, `reverb_decay`, `reverb_damping`, `reverb_mix`, `reverb_bypass`
- **Configuration:**
  - `juce::dsp::Reverb::Parameters` struct updated each block from APVTS values:

  **Plate preset mapping:**
  - `roomSize`: mapped from `reverb_decay` — `roomSize = 0.4f + (decay_normalized * 0.55f)` (range ~0.4–0.95)
  - `damping`: `reverb_damping / 100.0f` (0–1.0)
  - `width`: 1.0f (full stereo spread — plate reverbs are wide)
  - `wetLevel`: 1.0f (dry/wet handled by separate DryWetMixer)
  - `dryLevel`: 0.0f
  - `freezeMode`: false

  **Room preset mapping:**
  - `roomSize`: mapped from `reverb_decay` — `roomSize = 0.1f + (decay_normalized * 0.50f)` (range ~0.1–0.60, shorter room)
  - `damping`: `reverb_damping / 100.0f`
  - `width`: 0.7f (slightly narrower than plate — more mono-compatible)
  - `wetLevel`: 1.0f
  - `dryLevel`: 0.0f
  - `freezeMode`: false

  - `decay_normalized = (decay_s - 0.3f) / (8.0f - 0.3f)` — maps 0.3–8.0s to 0.0–1.0
  - Process spec: stereo (2 channels), sized for max block
  - Module: `juce_dsp` required
  - CRITICAL: Use `juce::dsp::ProcessSpec` + `reverb.prepare(spec)` + `reverb.process(context)` — NOT `setSampleRate()` or `processMono()` (see critical pattern #17)

### 12. Reverb Wet/Dry Mixer

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer<float>`
- **Purpose:** Blend dry stereo signal with reverb wet signal
- **Parameters Affected:** `reverb_mix`
- **Configuration:**
  - Mix range: 0–100% maps to 0.0–1.0 wet proportion
  - Uses `MixingRule::linear`
  - Operates in stereo (2 channels)
  - Dry signal captured BEFORE pre-delay and reverb processing

### 13. Mono-to-Stereo Expander

- **JUCE Class:** Custom implementation (buffer copy)
- **Purpose:** Expand the mono compressor output to stereo for delay/reverb sections
- **Configuration:**
  - At the transition point (after compressor, before delay), the mono buffer is duplicated to both L and R channels
  - Delay processes L and R with the same input but independent delay lines (for potential future stereo delay)
  - For v1.0: delay processes in mono (single DelayLine), output copied to both channels
  - Reverb processes in stereo (inherently stereo juce::dsp::Reverb)

## Processing Chain

```
[Mono Input - channel 0 only]
        |
        v
  +-----------+
  |  EQ Block |  <-- eq_hp_freq, eq_low_shelf_gain/freq,
  |           |      eq_mid_gain/freq/q, eq_high_shelf_gain/freq
  | HP Filter |
  | Low Shelf |      eq_bypass: if true, skip entire EQ block
  | Mid Peak  |
  | Hi Shelf  |
  +-----------+
        |
        v
  +-----------+
  | Compressor|  <-- comp_mode, comp_amount (Simple)
  |  (Mono)  |      comp_threshold/ratio/attack/release (Manual)
  |           |      comp_makeup
  |           |      comp_bypass: if true, skip compressor
  +-----------+
        |
        |--- [GR Meter] --> std::atomic<float> grMeterValue (audio thread write)
        |
        v
  [Mono→Stereo: copy ch0 to ch1]
        |
        v
  +-----------+
  |   Delay   |  <-- delay_mode (Slapback/Sync)
  |  (Mono,   |      delay_time (Slapback) or delay_division + BPM (Sync)
  | same sig  |      delay_feedback, delay_bypass
  | on L+R)   |
  +----+------+
       |
       +----> [Delay wet signal * delay_reverb_send] ---+
       |                                                |
       v                                                v
  +-----------+                                  [Reverb Input]
  | Delay D/W |  <-- delay_mix                         |
  |  Mixer    |                                         |
  +-----------+                                         |
       |                                               /
       +------[dry vocal stereo]                      /
              +-- [delay wet] (blended)              /
                                                    /
        v (stereo summed with send signal)----------+
  +-----------+
  | Pre-Delay |  <-- reverb_predelay (stereo, 0-100ms)
  |  (Stereo) |
  +-----------+
        |
        v
  +-----------+
  |  Reverb   |  <-- reverb_type (Plate/Room: parameter mapping)
  |  Engine   |      reverb_decay, reverb_damping
  | (Stereo)  |      reverb_bypass: if true, skip reverb + pre-delay
  +-----------+
        |
        v
  +-----------+
  | Reverb D/W|  <-- reverb_mix
  |  Mixer    |
  +-----------+
        |
        v
[Stereo Output - channels 0+1]
```

**Routing notes:**
- EQ and Compressor process mono channel 0 only (AudioBuffer has 2 channels but only ch0 written)
- After compressor: ch0 copied to ch1 (mono-to-stereo expansion)
- Delay: runs on ch0 (or two independent delay instances for L/R - same input, identical output for v1.0)
- Delay-to-Reverb send: taps the delay wet signal (before delay D/W mix) and scales by `delay_reverb_send`
- Reverb input = (vocal mono signal copied to stereo) + (delay send signal)
- When delay_bypass is true: delay_reverb_send has no effect (no delay output to send)
- Bypass switching: block-level (not sample-accurate) to keep implementation simple and stable

## System Architecture

### State Persistence

**What state is saved:**
- All 30 APVTS parameters (automatic via AudioProcessorValueTreeState)
- No non-APVTS custom state required (no folder paths, no lock states)
- 3 starter presets: "Pop Vocal", "Rock Vocal", "Intimate"

**JUCE classes:**
- `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState` — All parameter persistence (automatic)

**Save/restore methods:**
- `getStateInformation(MemoryBlock& destData)` — call `apvts.state.createXml()` then `copyXmlToBinary()`
- `setStateInformation(const void* data, int sizeInBytes)` — call `getXmlFromBinary()` then `apvts.state.copyPropertiesAndChildrenFrom()`

**Restore behavior:**
- Invalid/missing state: APVTS uses parameter defaults
- Version migration: not needed for v1.0 (no schema versioning required)

### GR Meter Data Flow (UI ↔ Audio Thread)

**Audio thread:**
- After compressor processBlock, compute gain reduction: `gr_dB = 20.0f * std::log10(output_rms / input_rms)` or read from compressor directly
- Write to `std::atomic<float> grMeterValue` (clamped 0 to -30 dB)

**Message thread (UI Timer):**
- `juce::Timer` fires at 30 Hz in PluginEditor
- Reads `grMeterValue.load()` and sends to JavaScript via `webView->evaluateJavascript()`
- JavaScript uses requestAnimationFrame loop for ballistic VU needle animation (see critical pattern #20)

| eq_low_shelf_freq | Float | 60–400 Hz | 200 Hz | Low Shelf | Frequency for makeLowShelf() |

| comp_release | Float | 10–1000 ms | 200 ms | Compressor | Manual mode: release time |
| comp_makeup | Float | 0–24 dB | 0 dB | Makeup Gain | Post-compressor linear gain |
| comp_bypass | Bool | false/true | false | Compressor | If true, bypass entire compressor |

| delay_mix | Float | 0–100% | 30% | Delay D/W Mixer | Wet proportion |

| reverb_predelay | Float | 0–100 ms | 20 ms | Pre-Delay | Pre-delay length before reverb tail |
| reverb_decay | Float | 0.3–8.0 s | 1.5 s | Reverb Engine | Maps to roomSize parameter |
| reverb_damping | Float | 0–100% | 50% | Reverb Engine | Maps to damping parameter |
| reverb_mix | Float | 0–100% | 25% | Reverb D/W Mixer | Reverb wet proportion |
| reverb_bypass | Bool | false/true | false | Reverb Engine | If true, bypass pre-delay + reverb |

## Algorithm Details

### Semi-Parametric EQ (4 biquad filters in series)

**Algorithm:** Direct Form II biquad IIR filter chain

**Implementation notes:**
- Use `juce::dsp::ProcessorChain` is NOT recommended here because the chain cannot be partially bypassed at the per-filter level; instead, maintain 4 separate `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>` instances in a C-style array or struct
- Update coefficients at the start of each `processBlock()` if parameter values changed (compare previous values vs current, or always update — overhead is negligible for 4 filters)
- Coefficient calculation formula (JUCE's built-in static methods):
  - HP: `*hpFilter.coefficients = *juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makeHighPass(sampleRate, eq_hp_freq)`
  - Low shelf: `*lsFilter.coefficients = *juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makeLowShelf(sampleRate, freq, 0.7071f, juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain(gain_dB))`
  - Mid peak: `*midFilter.coefficients = *juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makePeakFilter(sampleRate, freq, q, juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain(gain_dB))`
  - High shelf: `*hsFilter.coefficients = *juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makeHighShelf(sampleRate, freq, 0.7071f, juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain(gain_dB))`
- EQ bypass: check `eq_bypass` parameter at start of block; if true, skip all 4 filter process() calls
- Reset filter states in `prepareToPlay()` with `reset()`
- Filter state reset on large parameter jumps is NOT required (EQ parameters are smooth-swept by user)

### VCA Compressor (Simple Mode Parameter Mapping)

**Algorithm:** Feed-forward peak compression with exponential attack/release

**Implementation notes:**
- `juce::dsp::Compressor<float>` uses feed-forward envelope detection internally
- Simple mode formula:
  - `amount_normalized = comp_amount / 100.0f` (0.0–1.0)
  - `threshold_dB = -6.0f - (amount_normalized * 34.0f)` → range: -6 dB (amount=0) to -40 dB (amount=100%)
  - `ratio = 2.0f + (amount_normalized * 8.0f)` → range: 2:1 (gentle) to 10:1 (heavy)
  - Attack = 10ms (fixed), Release = 200ms (fixed) in Simple mode
- Manual mode: directly use `comp_threshold`, `comp_ratio`, `comp_attack`, `comp_release`
- Makeup gain: `outputGain = juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain(comp_makeup)` applied as multiply after compressor
- In both modes, call `compressor.setThreshold(threshold_dB)`, `compressor.setRatio(ratio)`, etc. at start of each block
- GR measurement: compare input RMS vs output RMS per block, store to `grMeterValue` atomic

### Delay Line (Circular Buffer)

**Algorithm:** Single-tap circular buffer delay with linear interpolation

**Implementation notes:**
- `juce::dsp::DelayLine` manages the circular buffer internally
- Set delay in samples: `delayLine.setDelay(delaySamples)` at block start
- delaySamples = `delayTimeMs * sampleRate / 1000.0f`
- Sync mode BPM calculation: `juce::AudioPlayHead::PositionInfo info; if (playHead && playHead->getPosition().hasValue()) { bpm = info.getBpm().orFallback(120.0); }`
- Note division multipliers: `{1/16: 0.25, 1/8: 0.5, 1/4: 1.0, 1/2: 2.0}` × `(60000 / bpm)` ms
- Feedback loop: maintain a `feedbackSample` float; for each sample: `inputWithFeedback = dryMono + feedbackSample; delayLine.pushSample(0, inputWithFeedback); wetSample = delayLine.popSample(0); feedbackSample = wetSample * (delay_feedback/100.0f);`
- Delay wet signal also routed to `reverbSendBuffer` after multiplying by `delay_reverb_send/100.0f`

### Delay-to-Reverb Send

**Algorithm:** Parallel signal routing via temporary accumulation buffer

**Implementation notes:**
- Allocate `juce::AudioBuffer<float> reverbSendBuffer(1, maxBlockSize)` in `prepareToPlay()`
- During delay processing: for each sample, `reverbSendBuffer.setSample(0, n, delaySend)` where `delaySend = wetSample * (delay_reverb_send/100.0f)`
- When delay is bypassed: zero out `reverbSendBuffer` before reverb processing
- Reverb input = mono signal (from compressor output) PLUS `reverbSendBuffer` mixed in
- This implements a classic "delay feeds into reverb" studio routing

### Reverb Pre-Delay

**Algorithm:** Short delay line applied before reverb input (stereo)

**Implementation notes:**
- Two `juce::dsp::DelayLine` instances (L + R) for stereo pre-delay
- Both L and R receive identical mono signal input (pre-delay does not create stereo differences)
- Set delay: `preDelayL.setDelay(reverb_predelay * sampleRate / 1000.0f)`
- Pre-delay is part of the "reverb bypass" block: when `reverb_bypass` is true, skip both pre-delay and reverb

### Reverb Parameter Mapping (Plate vs Room)

**Algorithm:** `juce::dsp::Reverb` with preset-specific parameter curves

**Implementation notes:**
- `juce::dsp::Reverb::Parameters params;`
- `decay_normalized = (reverb_decay - 0.3f) / (8.0f - 0.3f);` — normalized 0.0–1.0
- Plate: `params.roomSize = 0.4f + decay_normalized * 0.55f;` (0.40–0.95, longer, brighter tail)
- Room: `params.roomSize = 0.1f + decay_normalized * 0.50f;` (0.10–0.60, shorter, denser)
- Both: `params.damping = reverb_damping / 100.0f;`
- Plate: `params.width = 1.0f;` / Room: `params.width = 0.7f;`
- Always: `params.wetLevel = 1.0f; params.dryLevel = 0.0f;` (wet/dry handled by DryWetMixer)
- Call `reverb.setParameters(params)` at start of each block

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies

- EQ → Compressor: EQ output is compressor input (sequential, EQ shapes spectral content before dynamics)
- Compressor → Delay: Compressor output is delay input (sequential, compressed vocal feeds delay)
- Delay wet signal → Reverb send: delay output (before D/W mixing) feeds reverb input additive path
- Compressor → Mono-to-Stereo: must expand before delay/reverb sections
- Pre-delay → Reverb: pre-delay output feeds reverb input (stereo)
- Reverb output → Reverb D/W Mixer: reverb wet mixed with pre-reverb dry capture

### Parameter Interactions

- `comp_mode` governs which comp parameters are active: Simple mode ignores `comp_threshold/ratio/attack/release`; Manual mode ignores `comp_amount`. Both modes still use `comp_makeup`.
- `delay_mode` governs whether `delay_time` or `delay_division` is used; both are always in APVTS, but only one is used per block.
- `delay_bypass` disables `delay_reverb_send` (no signal to send)
- `reverb_type` changes the parameter mapping curves for `reverb_decay` and `width`; all other reverb parameters apply in both types
- High `delay_feedback` (>80%) can cause level buildup — capped at 90% in parameter range for safety
- High `delay_reverb_send` + high `reverb_mix` creates a lush "delay through reverb" effect; both are intentional design choices

### Processing Order Requirements

1. **Read dry input (ch0):** Capture before any processing
2. **EQ processing (mono ch0):** HP → Low Shelf → Mid Peak → High Shelf
   - Skip if `eq_bypass == true`
3. **Compressor processing (mono ch0):** Simple or Manual mode
   - Measure input RMS before processing
   - Process through `juce::dsp::Compressor`
   - Apply makeup gain
   - Measure output RMS, compute GR, write to `grMeterValue` atomic
   - Skip if `comp_bypass == true`
4. **Mono-to-Stereo expansion:** Copy ch0 to ch1
5. **Delay processing (mono or L+R with same signal):**
   - Compute delay time (Slapback or Sync)
   - Run feedback loop with DelayLine
   - Capture delay wet signal for reverb send
   - Apply `delay_reverb_send` scaling → write to `reverbSendBuffer`
   - Skip all if `delay_bypass == true` (zero `reverbSendBuffer`)
6. **Delay D/W mix:** Blend delayed with dry stereo signal
7. **Accumulate reverb input:** stereo from delay D/W + mono reverbSendBuffer added to both L+R
8. **Pre-delay (stereo):** Apply pre-delay to reverb input
   - Skip if `reverb_bypass == true`
9. **Reverb engine (stereo):** Apply `juce::dsp::Reverb` with preset parameters
   - Skip if `reverb_bypass == true`
10. **Reverb D/W mix:** Blend reverb output with dry stereo capture (from pre step 8)
    - Dry signal for reverb mix was captured before pre-delay
    - Skip if `reverb_bypass == true` (output = dry)

**Why this order matters:**
- EQ before compressor: industry-standard (pre-EQ shapes dynamics behavior, not post)
- Compressor before delay: prevents feedback from pumping the compressor
- Delay before reverb: allows delay echoes to bloom in reverb space (studio standard)
- Delay D/W before reverb input accumulation: allows send level to be independent of delay mix

### Thread Boundaries

**Audio thread (processBlock):**
- All DSP: EQ, Compressor, Delay, Reverb, mixing
- APVTS parameter reads: `parameters.getRawParameterValue("id")->load()` (atomic)
- GR meter write: `grMeterValue.store(value)` (atomic float)
- BPM query: `getPlayHead()->getPosition()` (safe in audio thread)
- NO memory allocation, NO locks, NO file I/O

**Message thread (UI Timer + editor):**
- GR meter read: `grMeterValue.load()` every ~33ms
- JavaScript GR level message send via `webView->evaluateJavascript()`
- Parameter updates via APVTS (automatic thread-safe mechanism)

**Communication:**
- APVTS: handles all parameter thread safety automatically
- GR meter: `std::atomic<float> grMeterValue` (lock-free atomic read/write)
- No other inter-thread communication needed

---

## Implementation Risks

### Semi-Parametric EQ (4 Biquad Filters)

**Complexity:** MEDIUM
**Risk Level:** LOW-MEDIUM

**Risk factors:**
- Coefficient recalculation uses JUCE static methods — well-supported, low artifact risk
- 4 separate filter instances slightly more verbose than ProcessorChain but necessary for bypass flexibility
- Potential for audio artifacts if filter states are reset unnecessarily on parameter changes (avoid unnecessary reset)

**Alternative approaches:**
1. `juce::dsp::ProcessorChain` with all 4 filters: simpler code, but harder to bypass individual filters and to conditionally update coefficients
2. Custom biquad implementation: more control but unnecessary given JUCE's IIR support

**Fallback architecture:**
- If IIR coefficient methods cause issues: fall back to `juce::dsp::ProcessorChain<IIR, IIR, IIR, IIR>` with always-on processing (bypass still possible at block level)

**Mitigation strategy:**
- Use JUCE's static coefficient helpers (well-tested)
- Test with sweeping eq_mid_freq rapidly (most common coefficient update scenario)
- Don't reset filter state on parameter change (only on prepareToPlay)

### Compressor (Simple/Manual Mode Switching)

**Complexity:** MEDIUM
**Risk Level:** LOW-MEDIUM

**Risk factors:**
- Simple mode formula must produce musically useful results (not just mathematically correct)
- Mode switching mid-playback could cause level jumps if parameters differ significantly
- `juce::dsp::Compressor<float>` may not expose internal envelope state for GR metering

**Alternative approaches:**
1. Two separate compressor instances (one per mode): cleaner separation but 2x DSP overhead
2. Manual implementation of VCA-style compressor: full control, but significantly more code

**Fallback architecture:**
- If `juce::dsp::Compressor` GR measurement not available: compute GR from RMS in/out ratio per block
- If Simple mode mapping feels wrong: adjust formula constants (threshold/ratio curves) during tuning

**Mitigation strategy:**
- Test Simple mode at 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% against vocals to verify musical response
- Use RMS input/output ratio for GR rather than internal compressor state

### Tempo-Sync Delay (AudioPlayHead)

**Complexity:** MEDIUM
**Risk Level:** MEDIUM

**Risk factors:**
- AudioPlayHead may not always be available (standalone mode, some DAWs)
- BPM may change mid-block (tempo automation) causing subtle time discontinuities
- Delay time change during playback can click if not smoothed

**Alternative approaches:**
1. Hard-code fallback BPM: 120 BPM when AudioPlayHead unavailable
2. Smooth delay time changes over a block (linear interpolation of delaySamples)

**Fallback architecture:**
- If AudioPlayHead unavailable: use fallback BPM = 120, log warning once
- If delay time changes cause clicking: implement sample-count-based delay time smoothing

**Mitigation strategy:**
- Wrap all AudioPlayHead calls in null checks
- Test in standalone (no host) and verify 120 BPM fallback works
- For v1.0: block-level delay time update is acceptable (no per-sample interpolation needed)

### Delay-to-Reverb Send Routing

**Complexity:** MEDIUM
**Risk Level:** LOW

**Risk factors:**
- Signal path is slightly non-standard; implementation details (pre vs post D/W mix) affect the sonic result
- Accumulation buffer must be sized correctly in prepareToPlay()

**Rationale for design choice:**
- Send is from delay wet signal (before delay D/W mix) so that `delay_mix` and `delay_reverb_send` are independent controls
- This matches professional routing (e.g., UAD Topline Vocal Suite, SSL 4000 send architecture)

**Fallback architecture:**
- If pre-D/W send causes confusion: move send to post-D/W (simpler routing, slightly different sound)

### Reverb Engine (juce::dsp::Reverb)

**Complexity:** LOW-MEDIUM
**Risk Level:** LOW

**Risk factors:**
- `juce::dsp::Reverb` parameter range for `roomSize` (0.0–1.0) doesn't map linearly to perceptual decay time — requires tuning of the mapping curves
- Plate vs Room distinction is parameter-mapping-only (same underlying algorithm) — sonic difference may be subtle
- CRITICAL: must use `prepare(spec)` + `process(context)` not old-style API (see critical pattern #17)

**Alternative approaches:**
1. Custom Freeverb implementation: more control over Plate/Room character but significantly more code
2. Two separate reverb instances (one per type): cleaner but 2x memory overhead
3. Third-party reverb library: adds dependency, not warranted for this application

**Fallback architecture:**
- If Plate/Room parameter maps are too similar: implement tone/character filter (simple shelf) after reverb for each type to create more distinct character
- If `juce::dsp::Reverb` quality insufficient: implement simple Schroeder reverb (4 comb + 2 allpass)

**Mitigation strategy:**
- Test Plate mapping (roomSize 0.4–0.95) vs Room mapping (0.1–0.60) with typical vocal signals
- Tune damping and width differences to maximize Plate/Room distinction
- ALWAYS use ProcessSpec pattern, never old API

### GR Meter (UI Thread Synchronization)

**Complexity:** LOW
**Risk Level:** LOW

**Risk factors:**
- Atomic float read on message thread vs audio thread write: safe by design
- Timer rate (30 Hz) must not overwhelm UI thread
- JavaScript requestAnimationFrame + ballistic interpolation adds visual complexity

**Mitigation strategy:**
- Use `std::atomic<float>` for grMeterValue (lock-free, no mutex needed)
- Use 30 Hz update rate (not 60 Hz — prevents UI starvation)
- Follow critical pattern #20 (requestAnimationFrame + ballistic motion)

### Mono-in / Stereo-out Bus Configuration

**Complexity:** LOW
**Risk Level:** LOW

**Risk factors:**
- Bus configuration requires careful setup in AudioProcessor constructor
- `BusesProperties` must include mono input + stereo output — some DAWs may not pass mono input correctly

**CRITICAL:** Bus configuration pattern (from critical patterns #4):
```cpp
AudioProcessor(BusesProperties()
    .withInput("Input",  juce::AudioChannelSet::mono(),   true)
    .withOutput("Output", juce::AudioChannelSet::stereo(), true))
```
- This is an EFFECT (not IS_SYNTH) so both input and output buses are required
- The `isBusesLayoutSupported()` override should accept: mono-in + stereo-out

**Fallback architecture:**
- If mono input causes DAW issues: use stereo input, process ch0 only, copy to ch1 after comp

### Overall Project Risk

**Overall complexity:** MEDIUM-HIGH
- 4 DSP sections with interdependencies
- 30 parameters with mode-switching logic
- Mono-to-stereo routing with parallel send path
- GR meter requires UI-audio thread communication
- BPM sync requires AudioPlayHead integration

**Highest risk component:** Compressor (Simple mode mapping + GR metering)
- Requires musical tuning of parameter curves, not just implementation
- GR output requires atomic communication with UI

**Recommended approach:**
1. Start with EQ section (lowest risk, well-understood biquad filters)
2. Implement compressor with Simple mode only first, add Manual mode
3. Implement delay with Slapback mode first, add Sync mode
4. Implement reverb with Plate preset, verify parameter mapping, add Room
5. Integrate send routing last (after individual sections verified)
6. Add GR metering after audio processing works correctly

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: Mono Input + Stereo Output Bus Layout

**Decision:** Use mono input, stereo output (`AudioChannelSet::mono()` in, `AudioChannelSet::stereo()` out)

**Rationale:**
- Creative brief specifies mono-in/stereo-out format
- Vocal recordings are mono (single microphone)
- Stereo spread is an artistic choice, not a channel requirement
- EQ + Comp work in mono: signal processing efficiency

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Stereo input + stereo output: More DAW-compatible (no mono-in issues) but processes L+R unnecessarily through EQ/comp, wasting CPU and potentially creating phase issues if L≠R
2. Process both channels in mono style (ch0 only): Same result but less explicit; bus layout should match true signal flow

**Tradeoffs accepted:**
- Some DAWs may have minor issues with mono-in plugins; acceptable because vocal tracks are mono

### Decision: juce::dsp::Reverb for Both Plate and Room

**Decision:** Use single `juce::dsp::Reverb` instance with different parameter mappings for Plate vs Room types

**Rationale:**
- Implementing separate reverb algorithms (true plate vs true room) would require custom DSP (Schroeder/Moorer for room, FDN for plate) — significant development risk
- `juce::dsp::Reverb` provides adequate quality for a vocal channel strip (not a dedicated reverb plugin)
- Parameter mapping (different roomSize ranges + width) creates sufficient sonic distinction
- Single instance is CPU-efficient

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Two separate `juce::dsp::Reverb` instances (one per type): Cleaner but 2x memory, no sonic benefit
2. Custom Freeverb implementation: More control but significantly more code and risk
3. FDN (Feedback Delay Network): Highest quality but complex, requires significant DSP expertise

**Tradeoffs accepted:**
- Plate/Room distinction is parameter-map-only, not algorithm-based — sonic difference is subtle
- Professional plate reverbs (EMT 140) sound quite different from juce::dsp::Reverb; acceptable for channel strip context

### Decision: Block-Level Bypass Switching

**Decision:** Bypass switching is block-level (not sample-accurate)

**Rationale:**
- Sample-accurate bypass requires crossfade buffers and additional complexity
- Block-level bypass has negligible audible difference for user-initiated switching
- Professional channel strips (SSL 4000) use relay-based bypass which is also block-level equivalent

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Sample-accurate bypass with crossfade: Professional quality but significant implementation complexity (50-100ms crossfade buffer per bypassed section)
2. DryWetMixer approach for bypass: Uses JUCE's latency compensation but adds 4 DryWetMixers (one per section)

**Tradeoffs accepted:**
- Small audio click possible when bypass is toggled during playback at high volume — acceptable for v1.0

### Decision: Delay-to-Reverb Send Pre-D/W Mix

**Decision:** Send tap occurs BEFORE delay wet/dry mixing (pure delay wet signal)

**Rationale:**
- Allows `delay_mix` and `delay_reverb_send` to be fully independent controls
- Matches SSL 4000 send architecture (sends are pre-fader in channel strip context)
- Professional engineers expect delay send to be independent of delay return level

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Post-D/W send: Simpler implementation but `delay_mix=0%` would also silence the reverb send
2. Pre-D/W with normalization: Unnecessary complexity

### Decision: Simple Mode Compressor Mapping Formula

**Decision:** threshold_dB = -6.0 - (amount * 34.0), ratio = 2.0 + (amount * 8.0)

**Rationale:**
- Inspired by Voxengo Voxformer one-knob compressor approach
- At 0%: very gentle (-6 dB threshold, 2:1 ratio) — barely noticeable compression
- At 50%: -23 dB threshold, 6:1 ratio — typical vocal compression
- At 100%: -40 dB threshold, 10:1 ratio — heavy limiting

**Alternatives considered:**
1. Logarithmic amount curve: May feel more natural but harder to tune without real-time A/B testing
2. Attack/Release also variable with Amount: More complex, risk of unwanted character changes

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety

- All parameter reads use `parameters.getRawParameterValue("id")->load()` in processBlock (atomic reads)
- GR metering uses `std::atomic<float> grMeterValue` — lock-free, no mutex
- No background threads needed (no file I/O)
- BPM read in audio thread via `getPlayHead()` — JUCE guarantees this is safe in processBlock

### Performance

- EQ (4 biquad filters): ~3–5% CPU at 48kHz
- Compressor (juce::dsp::Compressor): ~5–8% CPU
- Delay (juce::dsp::DelayLine with feedback): ~5% CPU
- Reverb (juce::dsp::Reverb, stereo): ~20–30% CPU
- Total estimated: ~35–50% single core at 48kHz (acceptable for channel strip)
- Optimization: Parameter reads cached at block start, not per-sample

### Denormal Protection

- Use `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` at top of `processBlock()`
- All `juce::dsp::` components handle denormals internally
- Feedback loop (delay) susceptible to denormals at near-silence: ScopedNoDenormals covers this

### Sample Rate Handling

- All juce::dsp components reconfigured in `prepareToPlay()` via `ProcessSpec`
- EQ coefficients recalculated in `prepareToPlay()` (sample rate dependency)
- Delay line buffer sized for maximum expected rate (1000ms at 192kHz = 192000 samples)
- Pre-delay buffer sized for 100ms at 192kHz = 19200 samples
- Reverb reinitialized with new spec in `prepareToPlay()`

### Latency

- EQ + Compressor: 0 samples latency (no lookahead)
- Delay: user-controlled (not counted as plugin latency)
- Reverb: 0 samples latency (no lookahead)
- Pre-delay: user-controlled (not plugin latency)
- **Total reported latency:** 0 samples (`getLatencySamples()` returns 0)
- Creative brief specifies "lookahead-free VCA compressor" — confirmed, no latency compensation needed

### CMake Requirements

```cmake
target_link_libraries(VocalStrip
    PRIVATE
        juce::juce_audio_utils
        juce::juce_audio_processors
        juce::juce_dsp           # Required: IIR filters, Compressor, DelayLine, Reverb, DryWetMixer
        juce::juce_gui_extra     # Required: WebBrowserComponent
)
juce_generate_juce_header(VocalStrip)  # CRITICAL: After target_link_libraries

target_compile_definitions(VocalStrip
    PUBLIC
        JUCE_WEB_BROWSER=1
        JUCE_USE_CURL=0
        JUCE_VST3_CAN_REPLACE_VST2=0
)
```

Plugin declaration:
```cmake
juce_add_plugin(VocalStrip
    FORMATS VST3 AU Standalone
    IS_SYNTH FALSE           # Effect (not instrument)
    NEEDS_MIDI_INPUT FALSE
    NEEDS_MIDI_OUTPUT FALSE
    NEEDS_WEB_BROWSER TRUE   # CRITICAL for WebView UI
    PLUGIN_CODE Vstr
    COMPANY_NAME "YourCompany"
    PLUGIN_MANUFACTURER_CODE Manu
    PRODUCT_NAME "VocalStrip"
)
```

## Research References

### Professional Plugins

1. **SSL 4000 Channel Strip (UAD/Native)**
   - Semi-parametric EQ: HP + 2 peak bands + 2 shelves in series (mono/stereo)
   - VCA compressor: side-chain filtering, fast attack, program-dependent release
   - Observed: HP at 80 Hz + high shelf at 10 kHz boost is standard vocal preset
   - EQ pre-comp configuration is classic SSL approach

2. **UAD Topline Vocal Suite**
   - Horizontal left-to-right signal flow (EQ → Comp → Delay → Reverb)
   - Delay→Reverb send slider: "Verb Send" control feeds delay into reverb
   - Simple/Manual toggle on compressor matches VocalStrip comp_mode design
   - Reverb: Plate + Room presets with predelay

3. **Voxengo Voxformer**
   - One-knob "Amount" compressor: internally maps to threshold + ratio
   - Amount 0% = 1:1 (no compression), 100% = heavy limiting (~10:1)
   - Served as direct inspiration for `comp_amount` Simple mode formula

4. **Lexicon 480L**
   - Plate algorithm: long decay (1–6s), wide stereo image, smooth tail
   - Room algorithm: shorter decay (0.3–2s), denser early reflections
   - Damping: high-frequency rolloff of reverb tail — standard parameter

5. **Waves CLA-2A / SSL G-Master Buss Compressor**
   - Reference for GR meter ballistic behavior: fast attack needle, slow return
   - VU needle style: -30 to 0 dB scale, with peak zone coloring

### JUCE Documentation

- **`juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>`**: Biquad filter; module `juce_dsp`; use static `Coefficients::make*()` helpers; reset state in prepareToPlay
- **`juce::dsp::Compressor<float>`**: VCA-style compressor; module `juce_dsp`; setThreshold/Ratio/Attack/Release then prepare(spec) then process(context)
- **`juce::dsp::DelayLine<float>`**: Circular buffer delay; module `juce_dsp`; set max delay in constructor, then setDelay() per block
- **`juce::dsp::Reverb`**: Algorithmic reverb (Freeverb-based); module `juce_dsp`; uses ProcessSpec; critical pattern #17 applies
- **`juce::dsp::DryWetMixer<float>`**: Latency-compensated dry/wet; module `juce_dsp`; pushDrySamples() before processing, mixWetSamples() after
- **`juce::AudioPlayHead`**: BPM access via `getPosition()->getBpm()`; available in processBlock; null-check required
- **CRITICAL pattern #17:** Use `prepare(spec)` + `process(context)` for ALL juce::dsp components (not old setSampleRate/processMono API)

### Technical Resources

- *DAFX: Digital Audio Effects* (Zolzer) — IIR filter design chapter, compressor design
- *Designing Audio Effect Plugins in C++* (Will Pirkle) — biquad filter implementation patterns
- *The Freeverb Algorithm* (Jezar at Dreampoint) — underlying algorithm for juce::dsp::Reverb
- SSL 4000 Series operator manual — EQ/compressor parameter ranges and signal flow reference
- *Hack Audio* (Eric Tarr) — one-knob compressor design and mapping formulas

## Notes

- Plugin type: Audio Effect (IS_SYNTH FALSE)
- Bus layout: mono input + stereo output (requires `isBusesLayoutSupported()` override)
- GR metering: atomic float updated each processBlock, read by 30 Hz UI Timer
- Preset system: 3 starters ("Pop Vocal", "Rock Vocal", "Intimate") implemented in Validation stage
- All 4 section bypasses are independent and can be combined freely
- `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` wraps entire processBlock body
- Delay line max buffer: 1000ms at max sample rate; pre-delay max: 100ms
- Simple mode attack/release are fixed (not exposed in Simple mode): 10ms / 200ms
- Reverb DryWetMixer captures dry signal before pre-delay (before delay_reverb_send accumulation) to ensure clean dry signal in reverb mix
